notes: Read 2026-10-02 for markets US, CA, MX, GB, IE. Prices are numbers in the major unit of 'currency'. 'monthly'/'annual' are the regular (non-promotional) prices; promotions are in 'note'. 'taxIncluded' says whether the figure already contains sales tax / GST/HST / IVA / VAT; 'taxNote' says whether that comes from the page's own wording or from the market's legal pricing practice. A note marked SECONDARY means the figure came from a news or comparison site because the official page could not be read; LOW or MEDIUM CONFIDENCE is flagged likewise. null means not found, with the reason in 'note'.

Netflix sells no annual plans anywhere. Its help page carries a generic line that taxes may be added; UK and Irish consumer prices must include VAT by law, US and Canadian prices are before tax, and Mexican prices are shown IVA-inclusive under PROFECO rules.
HBO Max is not sold in Canada: HBO content streams on Crave (Bell Media). HBO Max launched in the UK and Ireland on 2026-03-26.
Crave's line-up changed on 2025-11-26 to a free tier, Standard With Ads and Premium; the older Basic / Standard / Premium Ad-Free trio no longer exists.

Price changes in 2026 captured here: Netflix US (26 Mar), PS5 worldwide (2 Apr), Xbox Game Pass Ultimate cut to $22.99 (21 Apr), Prime Video Ultra replaced Ad Free in the US (10 Apr), Spotify Canada (12 May), Apple Music US (July), Xbox consoles worldwide (1 Aug), Switch 2 in the US, Canada, Mexico, UK and Ireland (1 Sep), Amazon Prime Mexico (September; renewals from 21 Oct), Disney+ US (23 Sep; existing subscribers from 21 Oct), UK TV Licence £180 (1 Apr).

Not found from any reliable source, left null: PS5 and Xbox console prices in Mexico (no official MXN price; the Microsoft Store in Mexico sells no hardware), Prime Video standalone in Ireland, Apple Music's annual Individual plan, Spotify Basic's current price, Disney+ annual for the ads tiers, Switch 2 bundle prices outside the US.

Ireland: no change to the €160 fee in 2026 and no move of collection away from An Post as of Citizens Information's page edited 2026-09-15; a technical working group reported to the Minister in June 2026 with no decision announced.

Time use: ATUS 2025 (released 2026-06-25) is the latest; it covers people 15 and over and lost diaries for 30 Sep to 11 Nov 2025 to the federal shutdown. ONS's latest is the March 2024 Online Time Use Survey dataset (adults 18 and over, UK-wide, experimental statistics); its last bulletin is September 2023. ONS does not publish participation for TV or gaming detail lines; the UK reading-participant figure is derived and marked so.
GB rows use the repository's market code GB for the United Kingdom; the TV Licence and ONS figures cover the whole UK.
